content.text: The file has one unexpected column, `member_phone`, which the profile labels as PHI. Its shape is uniform across all 24 rows with no empties, and the rest of the file matches the contract. This looks like a deliberate addition, so I'll add the column to the contract.

input.contract_yaml:
# Member eligibility from a (synthetic) payer: one row per member, one file per day.
# Generated from the Synthea patients by packs/healthcare/generators/eligibility.py.
feed: healthcare.eligibility
version: 2
owner: vendor-ops@example.com
description: >
  Daily full eligibility file: every enrolled member with their plan and coverage dates.
  All data is synthetic.
classification: restricted
source:
  channels: [minio, sftp, api]
  filename_pattern: "elig_*.csv"
  # The business date in the name (elig_YYYYMMDD.csv). It must be a real date, not after
  # the day the file was received, and at most 7 days before it; otherwise the file is
  # quarantined (FILE.NAME_DATE). A name with no digits takes the date it was received.
  filename_date:
    regex: "^elig_([0-9]+)"
    format: "%Y%m%d"
    max_days_before_received: 7
    max_days_after_received: 0
format: { type: csv, delimiter: ",", encoding: utf-8, header: true }
expected_arrival: { cron: "0 6 * * *", grace: 2h }
on_row_violation: quarantine_row
max_bad_row_ratio: 0.05          # above this, the whole file is rejected
min_rows: 1
columns:
  - { name: member_id, type: string, required: true, unique: true, pattern: "^M[0-9]{9}$" }
  - { name: first_name, type: string, required: true, phi: true }
  - { name: last_name, type: string, required: true, phi: true }
  - { name: member_phone, type: string, required: true, pattern: "^[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{4}$", phi: true }
  - { name: dob, type: date, required: true, min: "1900-01-01", max: today, phi: true }
  - { name: sex, type: string, required: true, allowed: [F, M, U] }
  - { name: plan_code, type: string, required: true, allowed: [HMO, PPO, EPO, HDHP] }
  - { name: coverage_start, type: date, required: true, min: "1990-01-01" }
  - { name: coverage_end, type: date, description: "Empty while coverage is open" }
  - name: patient_ref
    type: string
    description: The payer's link to the clinical record (here the Synthea patient id)
    phi: true

input.rationale: The file (elig_20261021.csv, sha b47716d2...) has one new column, member_phone, after last_name. The profile shows it is named usably, has the same shape in all 24 rows (999-9999), has no empty values, and is labelled PHI (phone number). The other nine declared columns are unchanged in name, order and type. This reads as a deliberate vendor addition, not a fault, so the contract adds it: type string, required (no empties in the sample, identifier role), pattern ^[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{4}$ from the observed shape, phi: true. Nothing is loosened: the validator reported no loosening. Version bumped 1 to 2. Dry run: 24 accepted, 0 rejected, file not rejected.

content.text:
- **What changed in the file:** a new column, `member_phone`, appears after `last_name`. Its values all have the shape 999-9999, none are empty, and the profile labels it PHI. The other declared columns are unchanged.
- **Contract change:** I added `member_phone` as a required string with pattern `^[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{4}$` and `phi: true`, and bumped the version from 1 to 2. Nothing was loosened, so the validator reported no loosening.
- **Dry run:** 24 accepted, 0 rejected, file not rejected. I submitted candidate `2f609a0a66c25318` for review.
- **Judgement call:** I treated the phone column as deliberate because the data is clean and consistent. Making it required is a choice I made from the profile's identifier role; a reviewer may prefer it optional.
